# Data Lakehouse

A **data lakehouse** is a modern data architecture that combines the best features of **data lakes** and **data warehouses** into a single platform.

## Key Concepts

### Data Warehouse
- Stores **structured, processed** data
- Optimized for SQL queries and BI/analytics
- Strong ACID transactions, schema enforcement, and governance
- Typically expensive to scale
- Examples: Snowflake, Amazon Redshift, Google BigQuery

### Data Lake
- Stores **raw data** in any format (structured, semi-structured, unstructured)
- Cheap, scalable storage (often object storage like S3)
- Great for data science and ML workloads
- Lacks governance, consistency, and performance for BI queries
- Examples: Hadoop HDFS, Amazon S3-based lakes

### Data Lakehouse
- Combines **cheap, flexible storage** of a data lake with the **management and performance features** of a data warehouse
- Examples: Databricks (Delta Lake), Apache Iceberg, Apache Hudi

## Key Differences

| Feature | Data Warehouse | Data Lake | Data Lakehouse |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Data types** | Structured | All types | All types |
| **ACID transactions** | ✅ Yes | ❌ No | ✅ Yes |
| **Schema enforcement** | ✅ Strict | ❌ Schema-on-read | ✅ Flexible |
| **Cost** | High | Low | Low–Moderate |
| **BI performance** | Excellent | Poor | Good–Excellent |
| **ML/DS support** | Limited | Excellent | Excellent |
| **Data governance** | Strong | Weak | Strong |
| **Storage format** | Proprietary | Open (Parquet, etc.) | Open (Parquet, etc.) |

## Why the Lakehouse Emerged

Traditionally, organizations maintained **both** a data lake and a data warehouse, creating:
- **Data duplication** and inconsistency
- **Complex ETL pipelines** to move data between systems
- **Higher costs** and maintenance burden

The lakehouse eliminates this **two-tier architecture** by adding a **metadata/transaction layer** (like Delta Lake or Iceberg) on top of open file formats in cheap object storage, enabling warehouse-like features directly on the lake.

## In Summary

> A data lakehouse gives you **one platform** that supports BI analytics, SQL queries, real-time data, and machine learning — all on low-cost, open storage with strong governance and reliability.
